The idea at the centre

Children have something
to bring to the world.
Let’s help them discover it.

An introduction to the cohort

A small community.
A bigger way of seeing.

Project Arche brings a deliberately selected group of up to 12 children, aged 5–9, into a shared space for inquiry and making. Over 16 weeks, they move through four connected labs: Design & Engineering, Futures, Culture, and Media.

Each lab opens a different way of understanding the world. Together, they help children connect what they can make with what they can imagine, how they live with others, and what they want to say.

The ambition reaches beyond the objects children produce. It is to help them become thoughtful builders: people who notice, ask, make, reflect, and contribute with care.

01 / Our mission

Make room for discovery.

To give children the space, tools, and guidance to turn curiosity into understanding—and understanding into things, stories, and possibilities that serve others.

02 / Our vision

A generation of thoughtful builders.

Children who grow into people capable of imagining better worlds, working with integrity, and helping renew the communities and cultures they belong to.

Growing as a whole person

What we build matters.
Who we become matters, too.

Learning to collaborate, care, and exercise good judgment is part of the programme. A daily, one-hour Village block makes space to practise life together, alongside the work of the labs.

Children return throughout the cohort to the speedcube, abacus, and spatial reasoning materials—building fluency through regular practice while their projects grow in complexity.
